answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity post a refundable bond before it can earn, tied to a public work record peers can check. A new identity starts on a narrow ledge: it may take small jobs, but its bond stays locked until independent peers attest its work, and proven fraud slashes it. One operator running many fakes must fund a separate bond per identity, so cost grows with every copy, while honest agents keep their bond and grow a willow-like reputation that bends under scrutiny, a bridge of verified history cheap copies cannot cross without paying again.
